name: MGA Entertainment
desc: American toy and entertainment company known for Bratz dolls, with European distribution partners and an Australian animation studio.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 9.15bn in 2020 (Wikipedia infobox); owned by Isaac Larian (82%) and Larian family (18%)
markets: Toys and dolls sold in North America, South America and Europe; acquired Australian studio Pixel Zoo (MGA Studios) in 2022.
rationale: Global toy brand owner competing with F1 partners Mattel and LEGO; F1 licensing and young family fans suit its collectibles lines.

name: Mammoth Brands (Harry's)
desc: Consumer packaged goods company owning Harry's razors and the Flamingo, Lume, Mando and Coterie personal care brands.
capacity_detail: Harry's total annual revenue about USD 750m in 2023 (Wikipedia); Mammoth Brands site lists Harry's as its first brand
markets: Sold online and through Target and Walmart stores in the United States; owns German razor blade maker Feintechnik.
rationale: Male-skewed grooming group facing Gillette, an F1 partner; F1's young US male audience suits razor and grooming brand building.

name: MathWorks
desc: Software developer whose main products MATLAB and Simulink support data analysis and simulation for engineers and scientists.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.5bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Engineering, science and education customers in more than 180 countries; about 6,500 employees (2023).
rationale: Simulation software brand could use F1's engineering showcase to reach automotive and aerospace engineers, as rival software firms do.

name: PacSun
desc: Californian surfwear-rooted retailer selling clothing and accessories to teens and young adults through stores and online.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 950m in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox); owned by PSEB (Golden Gate Capital)
markets: Mall stores and e-commerce across the United States aimed at teens and young adults.
rationale: Youth fashion retailer could tap F1's growing Gen Z US audience through merchandise collaborations, as fashion brands do with teams.

name: REI
desc: Consumer co-operative retailer of outdoor gear and clothing operating 194 stores in 44 US states.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.7bn in 2021 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: 194 retail stores in 44 US states plus online sales; about 15,000 employees (2022).
rationale: Large outdoor lifestyle co-op with national reach; weak motorsport fit, but US races reach affluent active consumers.

name: Raising Cane's
desc: Fast-food restaurant chain specialising in chicken fingers, ranked third in annual sales among US quick-service chicken chains.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 5.1bn per Wikipedia infobox (citing Forbes profile of founder Todd Graves); no year given
markets: Quick-service restaurants across the United States; over 65,000 employees in 2025.
rationale: Fast-growing chain with celebrity-led marketing; F1's US races and young fans could take the brand beyond its southern base.

name: Rooms To Go
desc: Furniture retailer operating 148 showrooms in ten US states from Virginia to Texas, plus Tennessee.
capacity_detail: US furniture and bedding sales USD 3,278.1m in 2025 (Home News Now 125 ranking); Wikipedia gives USD 3.8bn for 2022
markets: Showrooms along the US coast from Virginia to Texas and in Tennessee, with Northern Virginia openings planned.
rationale: Major Florida and Texas furniture retailer; the Miami and Austin Grands Prix sit in its core markets for hospitality and activation.

name: J. R. Simplot Company
desc: Agribusiness group best known for frozen French fries and potato processing, which bought Belgium's Clarebout Potatoes in 2025.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 6.0bn in 2020 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Potato processing in the United States, including Ontario, Oregon, plus Clarebout Potatoes in Belgium since 2025.
rationale: B2B food supplier with a new European base; F1 hospitality could support global quick-service restaurant client relationships.

name: Suffolk Construction
desc: Construction management and general contracting firm delivering large building projects across the United States, ranked in ENR's Top 400.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 7.5bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox); ENR lists USD 5,330.4m for 2024
markets: US building construction markets, expanding into California through the 2011 ROEL Construction acquisition.
rationale: Contractor targeting USD 10bn revenue; F1 hospitality suits client entertainment, though consumer brand relevance is low.

name: Susquehanna International Group
desc: Privately held trading firm in options market making, proprietary trading and venture investing, including a large ByteDance stake.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 22.1bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Trades equities and options on US exchanges such as CBOE, AMEX, PHLX and ISE; investor in ByteDance.
rationale: Quant trading firms use F1 technology partnerships for graduate recruitment and brand; SIG's scale could fund a top-tier deal.

name: Taylor Farms
desc: Producer of fresh-cut salads and vegetables supplying restaurant chains, retailers and distributors such as Chipotle, Costco and Sysco.
capacity_detail: Revenue above USD 7bn (milestone announced 2026; period unspecified, Wikipedia infobox)
markets: US foodservice and retail customers including Chipotle, Costco, Subway, Olive Garden and Sysco.
rationale: Large B2B fresh-food supplier; F1's US races offer client hospitality, but consumer brand fit is limited.

name: Total Wine & More
desc: Retail chain selling wine, spirits, beer and cigars through about 250 US superstores and online.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 6bn in 2023 (Forbes figure cited by Wikipedia)
markets: About 250 stores (2023) across the United States plus online ordering.
rationale: Leading drinks retailer; F1 drinks partners like Heineken and Moet could co-fund US race-weekend retail promotions with it.

name: Whataburger
desc: Texas fast-food burger chain with about 1,211 restaurants in 2026, also selling branded products in grocery stores.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.34bn in 2022 (Wikipedia infobox); majority owned by BDT & MSD Partners, Dobson family minority
markets: Restaurants in 14 US states (2022), concentrated in Texas, plus grocery retail products.
rationale: Texan icon; the US Grand Prix at Austin is home turf, making a race or team deal a regional brand play.

name: Tillamook County Creamery Association
desc: Farmer-owned Oregon dairy co-operative making cheese, ice cream, yogurt and butter, a top-50 North American dairy processor.
capacity_detail: Sales USD 1bn in 2021 (Dairy Foods, cited by Wikipedia)
markets: Dairy products sold across the United States from Oregon production.
rationale: Consumer dairy brand with mainly domestic reach; F1 fit limited to US race-weekend sampling and hospitality.

name: The Duckhorn Portfolio
desc: Napa Valley-founded premium wine company producing wines from California and Washington State, taken private in 2024.
capacity_detail: Bought by Butterfly Equity for about USD 1.95bn in December 2024 (Wikipedia)
markets: Wines from California and Washington State sold mainly in the United States.
rationale: Premium wine group seeking brand prestige; F1 hospitality pouring rights in the US races could showcase its luxury labels.

name: STO Building Group
desc: Building construction group ranked sixth on ENR's 2025 Top 400 Contractors list, mainly in general building.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 12,038.0m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: US general building construction, with USD 915m of international revenue reported to ENR for 2024.
rationale: Top-ten US builder with international work; F1 hospitality could support client entertainment in data-centre and commercial markets.

name: McCarthy Building Companies
desc: Employee-owned US construction firm, family-owned for 138 years, ranked 20th on ENR's 2025 Top 400 Contractors list.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 6,980.8m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025); McCarthy Holdings Inc.; 100% employee-owned per company site
markets: Construction projects across the United States, including the UC Davis Health California Tower in Sacramento.
rationale: Large employee-owned builder; F1 hospitality fits B2B client entertainment, though consumer brand value is low.

name: Mortenson
desc: Family-owned US construction company known for sports and entertainment venues, ranked 22nd on ENR's Top 400 Contractors.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 6,692.4m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: Construction across the United States, including over 230 sports and entertainment venues such as Allegiant Stadium.
rationale: Leading US sports-venue builder; the Las Vegas Grand Prix and venue clients make F1 hospitality commercially relevant.

name: Swinerton
desc: Employee-owned national construction firm providing commercial building, construction management, design-build and self-perform services.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 4,848.1m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: Commercial construction across the United States; company describes itself as a USD 5bn national firm.
rationale: Employee-owned national builder; F1 hospitality could serve West Coast client entertainment, with limited consumer relevance.

name: Michels Corporation
desc: Family-owned Wisconsin construction and infrastructure contractor ranked 38th on ENR's 2025 Top 400 Contractors list.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 4,078.6m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: Construction across the United States, plus USD 285.3m of international revenue reported to ENR for 2024.
rationale: Infrastructure contractor with international work; F1 offers client hospitality but little consumer brand value.

name: Moss Construction
desc: Florida-based construction firm ranked 41st on ENR's 2025 Top 400, building projects such as Fort Worth's Westside Village.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 3,709.6m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: US construction, including the USD 1.7bn Westside Village mixed-use district in Fort Worth.
rationale: Florida builder in the Miami Grand Prix home market; F1 hospitality could support developer and client relationships.

name: Turner Industries
desc: Louisiana industrial contractor providing construction and contract maintenance services, ranked 44th on ENR's 2025 Top 400 Contractors.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 3,214.8m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: Industrial construction and contract maintenance in the United States.
rationale: Industrial B2B contractor; F1's engineering image suits recruitment, but consumer brand relevance is low.

name: Shawmut Design and Construction
desc: Employee-owned construction management firm with 13 offices nationwide, ranked 61st on ENR's 2025 Top 400 Contractors.
capacity_detail: Total revenue USD 2,065.9m in 2024 (ENR Top 400 Contractors, May 2025)
markets: Construction projects across the United States from 13 offices, including growth in Rhode Island.
rationale: Employee-owned national builder; F1 hospitality suits client entertainment, though consumer brand reach is small.

name: Rosendin
desc: The largest employee-owned electrical contractor in the United States, founded as a family shop in San Jose in 1919.
capacity_detail: Average annual revenues of USD 5.6bn (company history page)
markets: Electrical contracting across the United States, founded in San Jose, with offices in Hawaii, Virginia, Maryland and Oregon.
rationale: Large national electrical contractor; F1 hospitality could support client relationships, with little consumer brand value.

name: Terracon
desc: Employee-owned engineering consultancy with more than 200 US locations, reporting USD 1.1bn revenue in 2023.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.1bn in 2023 (company About page timeline)
markets: More than 200 locations across the United States serving development and infrastructure projects.
rationale: B2B engineering consultancy with little consumer exposure; F1 mainly offers recruitment and client hospitality value.

name: Mathis Home
desc: Furniture and bedding retailer running Mathis Home, Design Studio, Mathis Sleep and Mathis Outlet stores in four states.
capacity_detail: US furniture and bedding sales USD 415.0m in 2025; total 2025 revenues USD 422m (Home News Now 125)
markets: Stores in Oklahoma, California, Texas and Arkansas, plus Ashley and La-Z-Boy licensed galleries.
rationale: Regional furniture retailer in Texas; the Austin Grand Prix offers local hospitality, but national F1 fit is weak.

name: Slumberland Furniture
desc: Midwestern furniture and mattress retailer with 119 showrooms in 12 states, 68 of them franchised.
capacity_detail: US furniture and bedding sales USD 406.0m in 2025; total 2025 revenues USD 410m (Home News Now 125)
markets: 119 showrooms across 12 Midwestern states, including 39 in Minnesota.
rationale: Regional Midwestern retailer; limited fit with F1's international audience beyond broadcast-led promotions.

name: Mattress Warehouse
desc: Bedding retailer operating Mattress Warehouse and Sleep Outfitters stores across eastern and midwestern US states, 531 stores in 2025.
capacity_detail: US furniture and bedding sales USD 395.0m in 2025, up 46.3% (Home News Now 125)
markets: Mattress Warehouse stores in 23 eastern and midwestern states; Sleep Outfitters in six states.
rationale: Fast-growing mattress chain; sleep-and-performance messaging could use F1 athletes, though reach is domestic.

name: Room & Board
desc: Employee-owned modern furniture and home furnishings retailer selling through 23 showrooms nationwide and online.
capacity_detail: US furniture sales USD 596.0m in 2025; total 2025 revenues USD 629m (Home News Now 125)
markets: 23 showrooms across the United States plus online sales; became an ESOP in 2024.
rationale: Design-led premium furniture brand; F1 design and lifestyle audiences fit, but national scale limits the budget.

name: doTERRA
desc: Direct-selling company offering essential oils, skin care, nutrition and wellness products through independent distributors.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2bn in 2024 (DSN Global 100 list, 2025 edition)
markets: Independent Wellness Advocates in about 100 countries; sourcing work in countries such as Bulgaria.
rationale: Global direct seller; F1 sponsorship would give its distributor network a premium, worldwide incentive and recognition platform.

name: Young Living Essential Oils
desc: Multi-level marketing company selling essential oils and home products through independent distributors, with 33 corporate offices.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.2bn in 2020 (DSN Global 100 list, 2021 edition)
markets: Sells essential oils and home products through independent distributors; listed as a US company in DSN's Global 100.
rationale: International direct seller; F1 could reward and motivate its distributor base, as wellness brands use motorsport hospitality.

name: Schreiber Foods
desc: Dairy foods company supplying retailers, restaurants, distributors and food manufacturers around the globe, with over 10,000 employees.
capacity_detail: Annual sales of more than USD 7bn (company About page, read Nov 2026; Forbes cited USD 7bn+ in 2016)
markets: Dairy products for retail, restaurant and food manufacturing customers in the US and around the globe.
rationale: Large B2B dairy supplier; F1 could support global foodservice client hospitality, but consumer brand fit is weak.

name: Ocean Spray
desc: Agricultural co-operative of about 700 family farmers producing cranberry juices and foods, covering 70% of North American cranberries.
capacity_detail: Sales USD 1.2bn in fiscal year 2013 (Wikipedia)
markets: Juices and cranberry products sold in the United States and abroad; sales in 50 countries by 1978.
rationale: Well-known beverage brand facing PepsiCo, an F1 partner; F1 could refresh its image with younger international consumers.

name: Monogram Foods
industry: packaged meat snacks and frozen foods
desc: Packaged foods maker producing meat snacks, frozen foods and appetisers, with 13 production facilities across the United States.
capacity_detail: Revenue surpassed USD 1bn (company Who We Are timeline; year not stated)
markets: Production plants in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Indiana, Iowa, Tennessee and other US states supplying US retail and foodservice.
rationale: Private-label and branded snack maker; F1 offers limited brand value beyond US race-weekend snack sampling.

name: Synechron
desc: Technology services and consulting company founded in New York in 2001, employing 16,000 people in 59 offices across 21 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue reached USD 1bn in fiscal year 2025 (company press release, 2 Sep 2025)
markets: 59 offices in 21 countries serving clients worldwide.
rationale: IT services rivals such as Cognizant, Globant and Mphasis already sponsor F1; Synechron could match them for client and talent branding.

name: Sargento
desc: Family-owned Wisconsin cheese company producing packaged food and dairy products, and a long-time sponsor in American motorsport.
capacity_detail: Sales over USD 1.8bn annually (Wikipedia infobox; no year given)
sponsorships: Long-time American motorsport sponsor, branded at Road America; title sponsor of a NASCAR Nationwide Series race at Road America
markets: Packaged cheese and dairy products sold across the United States.
rationale: Existing motorsport sponsor with Road America ties; F1's US growth could lift its trackside spending to a top-tier series.

name: Trek Bicycle
desc: American bicycle maker producing road and mountain bikes and Bontrager components, manufactured largely in Europe and Asia.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.0bn (Wikipedia infobox; no year given); parent Intrepid Corporation
sponsorships: Main sponsor of the Trek Factory Racing pro cycling team from 2014; earlier US Postal Service team
markets: Bicycles sold internationally; manufacturing in the Netherlands, Germany, Taiwan and China; owns Swiss Villiger and German Diamant.
rationale: Rival bike brand Specialized is already an F1 partner; Trek could use F1 to extend its pro-cycling performance marketing.

name: Waffle House
desc: Restaurant chain serving waffles, breakfast food and sandwiches, employing about 40,000 people at restaurants in the United States.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1bn (Wikipedia infobox, citing Forbes April 2021)
markets: Restaurants across the United States.
rationale: Domestic diner chain with cult status; F1 fit is weak beyond novelty activations at US races.

name: Wayne-Sanderson Farms
desc: Chicken producer formed by combining Sanderson Farms with Wayne Farms, controlled by a Cargill and Continental Grain joint venture.
ownership: joint venture: Cargill and Continental Grain
capacity_detail: Predecessor Sanderson Farms revenue USD 3.4bn in 2019 (Wikipedia infobox); combined company figure not found
markets: Chicken processing and sales in the United States.
rationale: Commodity poultry processor with little consumer branding; F1 relevance is very low.

name: Melaleuca
desc: Founder-owned mail-order direct seller with large international operations in Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and the UK.
capacity_detail: Gross sales USD 1.13bn in 2012 (Wikipedia article on founder Frank VanderSloot)
markets: United States plus Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom (about 25% of revenue in 2004).
rationale: Founder-led wellness seller with Asian markets; F1's strong Japanese and Australian audiences could support member recruitment there.
